local_copy.path: docs/papers/Causal Reasoning and Large Language Models Opening a New Frontier for Causality Kıcıman(2023).pdf

supported_claims: The paper proposes domain-knowledge-assisted graph drafts, graph critique and robustness suggestions while retaining formal causal analysis.
Its memorization test reports substantial completion of Tuebingen dataset cells; authors distinguish transforming known information from learning new causal structure.
Valid back-door inference remains conditional on the supplied graph; LLM-assisted adjustment and instrumental-variable suggestions are research directions.
limits: These are reported demonstrations and proposals, not a guarantee that an LLM supplies valid domain assumptions.
Training knowledge, new concepts and benchmark exposure constrain transfer; no bank-specific assignment or audit truth is established.

local_copy.path: docs/papers/CLadder Assessing Causal Reasoning in Language Models Jin(2023).pdf

supported_claims: CLadder generates more than 10,000 formal causal questions across three rungs, with commonsense, nonsensical and anti-commonsense verbalizations.
Table 2 reports GPT-4 accuracy 62.03% and CausalCoT 70.40% on dataset v1.5; all outcomes are paper-reported historical model results.
The authors identify language-to-formal-tool formulation as a remaining challenge even when a causal engine exists.
limits: Binary question accuracy does not measure bank identification validity, effect coverage or decision loss.
The benchmark covers selected graph/query families; natural-language paraphrases and anti-commonsense stories do not prove absence of all contamination.
Do not repeat unverified proprietary-model parameter counts from the experimental description.

local_copy.path: docs/papers/Large Language Models as Co-Pilots for Causal Inference in Medical Studies Alaa(2024).pdf

supported_claims: The proposed co-pilot follows a causal roadmap from the scientific question to assumptions, statistical estimands and interpretation.
Examples distinguish prevalent from incident users and specify eligibility, follow-up, baseline time, treatment and outcome; the paper discusses potentially time-varying exposure.
The authors find that careful cues help illustrative answers while off-the-shelf zero-shot responses may remain generic and miss relevant biases.
limits: This is a proposal with illustrative prompts, not a qualified longitudinal-policy implementation.
The paper itself identifies contamination uncertainty and missing study-design evaluations; medical-knowledge tests cannot substitute for study-design validity.
Transfer of these study-design principles to banking is a project proposal and needs owner-approved clocks and decisions.

local_copy.path: docs/papers/CausalDS Benchmarking Causal Reasoning in Data-Science Agents Leban(2026).pdf

supported_claims: CausalDS provides narrated synthetic SCM scenes, data files, a separate observation model and private scoring artifacts.
Interventional and counterfactual targets have separate identification decisions, with abstention on nonidentifiable tasks.
The paper reports a 100-scene exam sampled from 953 scenes and finds that symbolic success, interval quality, abstention and cost can diverge.
limits: Identification is defined for conceptual variables; the paper explicitly distinguishes their noisy observed proxies. An adapter must preserve this distinction.
The reported leaderboard is a dated author evaluation, not evidence of model performance or costs measured here.
A generated story with hidden ground truth is a useful test setting, but does not establish authentic bank semantic/assignment truth.

local_copy.path: docs/papers/A Human-Augmenting Agentic Workflow for Observational Causal Inference Chou(2026).pdf

supported_claims: oci-agent places an accountable human principal over actor/critic personas and reproducible notebooks using deterministic causal libraries.
It targets point-in-time effects under supplied unconfoundedness, with cross-fitted AIPW and design diagnostics.
Authors report 231 ACIC datasets, a ten-dataset scaffolding comparison, and disguised LaLonde evaluations; the critic declines most PSID replications for poor overlap.
limits: The Netflix deployment and benchmark outcomes are author-reported, not independently reproduced here.

Trimming by a propensity interval changes the target to a trimmed-population effect; the text calls it ATO, but overlap-weighted ATO uses a different weighting measure. Inspect the code before mapping that target.
Balance and overlap diagnostics cannot certify absence of unmeasured confounding. Selected critic-approved estimates do not automatically have conditional coverage.
Point-in-time estimation is not longitudinal policy identification; sequential positivity, treatment-confounder feedback and dependent sampling remain separate requirements.

supported_claims: Suggests confounders and relationships through language-model calls; suggest_backdoor delegates to the model suggester.
IdentificationSuggester.suggest_frontdoor is TODO/pass; SimpleIdentificationSuggester.suggest_frontdoor prompts for a factor list. Neither implements formal identification.
limits: Use only as a hypothesis-elicitation candidate; verify adjustment/ID with a formal engine.

additional_inspections.review_note: Distinguish IdentificationSuggester.suggest_frontdoor TODO/pass from SimpleIdentificationSuggester.suggest_frontdoor, which generates text suggestions and does not implement formal identification.

supported_claims: The population identification helper distinguishes identifiable true/false from unknown backend/error states.
It filters an IV estimand out of nonparametric population-ATE identification and can project explicit latent DAGs to y0 mixed graphs.
The README describes network-disabled task containers and separately network/model-enabled scene generation.
The grader gives abstention credit only for an explicitly abstainable task and an intentional null-equivalent response; malformed answers do not earn abstention credit.
The interval grader records width and coverage as well as an interval score; summary normalized interval scores are capped at 10.
The inspected helpers default missing identification metadata toward identifiable/not-nonidentifiable. The ATE interval branch checks ordering but does not explicitly reject every nonfinite endpoint.
limits: High-priority benchmark candidate after auditing scorer, observation-model semantics and original data/assumption identities.
Do not turn missing-backend unknown into nonidentification; preserve conceptual versus proxy variables.
No local reproduction or container-conformance claim yet.

Require an explicit three-state identification oracle and finite interval validation before scorer adoption; missing metadata must stay unknown. Report uncapped tail losses alongside any capped aggregate.
